items.title: Invasion Day bomb declared terror act, as accused's 'pro-white ideology' probed
items.description: The attempted bombing of an Invasion Day rally in Perth's CBD last week is declared a terrorist attack by authorities.

items.title: Gus disappearance declared major crime, suspect identified
items.description: South Australian police have declared the disappearance of Gus Lamont a major crime and say a person who lives at his outback property is now considered a suspect, but have stressed that the boy's parents are not under investigation.

items.title: Live: Alleged Perth attack motivated by white supremacist ideology: Burke
items.description: Australian human rights lawyer Chris Sidoti has called for Israeli President Isaac Herzog to be arrested in Australia for inciting genocide. Follow live.

items.title: Sydney 19yo charged over alleged death threat to Israel's Herzog
items.description: Darcy Tinning was arrested by AFP officers on Wednesday and charged with making a threat to kill an "internationally protected person".

items.title: Psychiatrist of Westfield Bondi Junction attacker referred for review by coroner
items.description: Findings from the coronial inquest into the Westfield Bondi Junction stabbing have been handed down, almost two years on from the attack.

items.title: Two months into the social media ban, a teenager says it's 'useless'
items.description: Australia's world-first social media ban for under-16s is two months old, but teenagers say they have found ways around it.

items.title: 'Groomed, coerced and threatened': Man faces 596 child abuse charges
items.description: A Queensland man has been charged with 596 child abuse-related offences after he allegedly "groomed, coerced and threatened" hundreds of young people.

items.title: This 'big, beautiful plan' has backfired, costing Timor-Leste hundreds of millions
items.description: The Greater Sunrise gas project was meant to transform Timor-Leste and bring billions in revenue, but locals are still waiting for the jobs and opportunities that were promised.

items.title: Bill shock still hitting patients after specialists' visits as calls mount for reforms
items.description: A survey of 4,000 patients finds more than half had an unexpected cost when under a specialist's care.

items.title: Australians in Japan shaken by ski deaths but say its snowfields are safe
items.description: Australians working in Japan's ski fields say while the sport has unpredictable risks, there are ways to be prepared.

items.title: Unions pushing 4 per cent wage boost as real paypackets decline
items.description: Australia's biggest employers are under pressure to give their workers pay increases above 4 per cent this year, as real wages go backwards and the union movement ramps up pressure.

items.title: Trump, tariffs, gold — how are Australia's biggest companies faring?
items.description: Australia's mining sector is expected to lead the earnings charge for this reporting season, boosted by signs of a stabilisation in the Chinese economy and a turbo-charged commodities market.

items.title: Strict caps on bottled water extraction urged for precious rainforest area
items.description: A long-awaited study warns that the extraction of bottled water from the World Heritage-listed Springbrook area poses a potential risk to the ancient Gondwana rainforests and should be strictly limited.

items.title: Capital gains tax reform among options as Labor weighs housing pitch
items.description: After Jim Chalmers repeatedly refused to rule out changing the capital gains tax discount, a government source told the ABC that changes related to housing were being considered, with capital gains not ruled out.

items.title: Owner who claimed Arnie the dog was stolen sentenced over German shepherd's death
items.description: A Queensland man who claimed his dog Arnie had been stolen, despite having left the German shepherd in his car, where it was later found dead, has pleaded guilty.

items.title: The zombie apocalypse devastates Tasmania in this soon-to-be cult classic
items.description: These Final Hours writer and director Zak Hilditch drew on personal tragedy to produce We Bury the Dead, his biggest cinematic epic yet.

items.title: Live: Silver plunges over 14 per cent as ACTU pushes above-inflation wages
items.description: Spot silver has hit a new low, crashing to $US75 an ounce, down over 14 per cent, while the ACTU is pushing for "above-inflation" wage increases in 2026. Follow the day's events and insights as they happen with our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Worker's death at Central Australian gold mine under investigation
items.description: A 47-year-old worker has died following an incident at the Tanami gold mine in remote Central Australia, with police and NT WorkSafe investigating.

items.title: CIA says it will cease publishing the CIA World Factbook
items.description: A statement on the CIA's website gives no reason for the decision, simply stating that the Factbook has been "sunset" while encouraging readers to "stay curious about the world and find ways to explore it".

items.title: AFL integrity unit looking into why police visited May
items.description: Melbourne veteran Steven May is being investigated by the AFL integrity unit, as the premiership defender stays away from Demons training.

items.title: Body-worn camera footage shows moment grandmother removed from birth suite
items.description: A confrontation caught on body-worn security footage in the halls of the Toowoomba Hospital maternity unit highlights concerns raised by local mothers.

items.title: Kiwi great backs State of Origin being played across the ditch
items.description: The NRL's reported landmark move to host a State of Origin match in New Zealand is hailed as "sensational" by Kiwi legend Gary Freeman.

items.title: Regulator probes charity status of 'apocalyptic Christian cult'
items.description: The Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission says it is investigating the charity status of Shincheonji, which featured prominently in the Victorian parliamentary inquiry into cults and fringe groups.

items.title: How Aussie bound for SuperBowl became NFL's best punter
items.description: Michael Dickson has become one of the finest punters in the NFL, and could become just the second Australian to play in a victorious Super Bowl team.

items.title: How a teenager who failed swimming lessons pulled off miracle ocean rescue
items.description: Austin Appelbee, 13, has made international headlines after swimming for four hours in rough seas to save his mum, sister and brother stranded in the ocean. How did he do it?
